1	# Voice
2	
3	## Tone Principles
4	
5	NINEONELABS copy should be:
6	
7	- Bold: confident, not arrogant.
8	- Experimental: surprising only when it improves clarity.
9	- Precise: no filler.
10	- Warm at scale: collaborative without becoming casual.
11	- Proof-driven: grounded in shipped work, systems, or measurable outcomes.
12	
13	Avoid:
14	
15	- generic agency speak
16	- empty inspiration
17	- technical name-dropping without outcome
18	- space fantasy without service clarity
19	- corporate boilerplate
20	- overly polite sales language
21	- trend-chasing AI/tool language
22	
23	## Korean Copy
24	
25	- Use formal polite public-facing Korean.
26	- Keep sentences short.
27	- Prefer `함께`, `여정`, `브랜드`, `설계`, `경험`, `구조`, `증명`.
28	- Avoid `솔루션`, `최고의`, `최적의`, `고객님`.
29	- A Korean line break must preserve grammar and meaning when each line is read alone.
30	
31	## English Copy
32	
33	- Display copy may use ALL CAPS or title case depending on visual role.
34	- English must be understandable to Korean readers at a glance.
35	- Prefer short, common words over clever phrasing.
36	- For clear utility/proof sections, use direct nouns first: `SERVICES`, `WORKS`, `PARTNERS`, `CLIENTS`, `CONTACT`.
37	- Do not force journey or space metaphors into section titles when the section job is already obvious.
38	- Avoid repeated `WE... / WE... / WE...` headline patterns unless repetition is the concept.
39	- Do not stack the same English opening shape across adjacent homepage sections when a stronger noun-led or outcome-led alternative exists.
40	- Vary openings with nouns, objects, outcomes, or fragments: `NEW WEBSITES`, `REAL WORK`, `FROM TEST TO LAUNCH`, `DESIGNED TO PROVE`, `BUILT THROUGH FRICTION`.
41	- Use `NINEONELABS` for public brand display. Use `nineonelabs` only in technical/code contexts.
42	
43	## Rhythm Rules
44	
45	Do not let consecutive sections use the same copy shape.
46	
47	| Scene | Copy Job | Suggested Shape |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| `intro` | invite | short English headline + 2 Korean lines |
50	| `introAction` | align and move | two short beats, each with a different verb |
51	| `hero` | land the slogan | slogan + short clarifying Korean line |
52	| `story` | reveal attitude | brand belief + concrete Korean proof |
53	
54	## Bad Copy And Better Direction
55	
56	| Do Not Write | Better Direction |
57	|---|---|
58	| `우리는 최고의 웹 경험을 제공합니다` | `우리가 만든 웹은 사용자가 스크롤을 멈추게 합니다` |
59	| `Innovative digital solutions` | `Scroll-triggered 3D brand story, built in Three.js` |
60	| `We are passionate about design` | `We ship design systems that work across 5 touchpoints` |
61	| `We use cutting-edge technology` | `Three.js, GSAP, and TypeScript embedded in the site you actually ship` |
62	| `브랜드의 가치를 높여드립니다` | `브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있을 때, 설계가 끝난 겁니다` |
63	
64	## Web Agency Copy Rules
65	
66	- Talk about results, not tools.
67	- Frame process as journey language only when it supports a concrete digital outcome.
68	- Every space metaphor must land on web, app, branding, UI/UX, maintenance, proof, or action.
69	
70	## Skill Label Rules
71	
72	- Skill labels in `why` may be short and technical, but descriptions must stay clear and outcome-aware.
73	- Use skill labels as proof signals, not service descriptions.
74	- Prefer compact pairs such as `THREE.JS / INTERACTIVE WEB`, `GSAP / MOTION & ANIMATION`, `CMS SYSTEM / CONTENT CONTROL`.
75	- If a skill description needs a full sentence, it probably belongs in `services` or a case study.

```markdown
| Word | Risk | Better Direction |
|---|---|---|
| familiar | too general; weak brand texture | default, ordinary, expected, uncharted |
| innovative | generic agency language | new, tested, built, proven |
| solution | corporate and vague | system, structure, website, build |
| future | vague unless grounded in service | launch, next screen, next orbit |
| mission | can become costume | project, build, structure, launch |
| universe | can feel like space fantasy | web experience, brand journey, orbit |

## Display Copy Guidance

- Use space words only when the next phrase grounds them in web, app, branding, UI/UX, maintenance, proof, or action.
- Prefer concrete digital words near metaphors: `web`, `screen`, `structure`, `system`, `launch`, `proof`.
- If Korean body copy is needed to explain an English headline, the English is too clever or too vague.
```

```markdown
# Service Manifests

Use this file when writing service, capability, proposal, or homepage service copy. Services must sound concrete, not like agency filler.

## WEB

### What It Is

Immersive websites, campaign pages, landing pages, brand sites, and Three.js interactive web experiences.

### Concrete Deliverables

- Site structure and page flow
- Responsive UI design
- Frontend implementation
- Interaction and motion system
- Three.js or scroll-based immersive scenes when useful
- Launch-ready production assets

### Best-Fit Client Situation

- A new brand needs a first public web presence.
- An existing brand needs a site that is remembered, not just visited.
- A campaign or product needs a focused digital launch.

### NINEONELABS Differentiator

We do not separate the brand story from the site. Strategy, interaction, motion, and implementation are designed as one web experience.

### Proof Signals

- Scroll-triggered interaction
- Production Three.js scene
- Fast, responsive implementation
- Clear conversion path
- Brand-specific visual system

### Korean Copy Direction

사람들이 느끼고 오래 기억하는 웹. 브랜드만의 구조와 인터랙션으로, 첫 화면부터 선택받을 이유를 설계합니다.

### What Not To Say

- 최고의 웹사이트
- 혁신적인 웹 솔루션
- 감각적인 홈페이지 제작

## APP

### What It Is

Mobile apps, PWAs, dashboards, hybrid app flows, and product interfaces that extend the brand beyond the website.

### Concrete Deliverables

- App flow and screen architecture
- UI/UX design
- Interactive prototype
- Frontend implementation plan or build
- Dashboard or user journey structure
- Handoff-ready design system when needed

### Best-Fit Client Situation

- A service needs a repeat-use user flow.
- A brand needs to live beyond a marketing site.
- Internal or customer-facing workflows need a clearer interface.

### NINEONELABS Differentiator

We design apps around behavior, not screen count. Every screen needs a job and every transition needs a reason.

### Proof Signals

- Clear user flow
- Reduced decision friction
- Responsive or hybrid architecture
- Reusable UI system
- Prototype-tested interactions

### Korean Copy Direction

브랜드는 화면 밖에서도 계속됩니다. 사용자가 다시 돌아올 수 있는 흐름과 구조를 중심으로 앱 경험을 설계합니다.

### What Not To Say

- 편리한 앱을 만들어드립니다
- 최신 기술 기반 앱 개발
- 모든 기능을 담은 앱

Naming, logo systems, visual language, brand guidelines, tone of voice, and identity systems that make the brand explainable.

- Naming direction
- Logo or logo system
- Color, type, and visual language
- Tone of voice
- Usage guidelines
- Web-ready identity application

### Best-Fit Client Situation

- A brand cannot explain itself in one sentence.
- The current identity feels generic or inconsistent.
- A web build needs a stronger brand system before design begins.

### NINEONELABS Differentiator

We build branding that survives the screen. Identity must work in web interaction, motion, UI, and real content.

### Proof Signals

- Clear brand sentence
- Consistent visual system
- Web-ready guideline
- Naming and tone consistency
- Cross-surface application

### Korean Copy Direction

브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있어야 합니다. 우리는 그 기준을 세우고, 어디서나 같은 인상이 남는 정체성을 만듭니다.

### What Not To Say

User flows, wireframes, prototypes, design systems, interaction logic, and screen structures that help users move naturally.
```
